author: Marcus
pages:
Dearest Livia,

They have posted us to a fort at the edge of the world. It snows in summer here. I am told this is a mild summer. The locals laugh at our cloaks and wear less clothing than I do in my bath.

The food is mostly elk, and the elk is mostly gristle. The ale is strong enough to strip paint. I have begun to like it, which worries me.

The Nords are not what I expected. They are loud and rude and drink before breakfast, but when the wolves came down on the supply wagons last week, the farmers grabbed pitchforks and ran out beside us without being asked. One old woman killed a wolf with a frying pan. She then cooked it in the same pan. I am still thinking about this.

Tell mother I am eating well. Do not tell her about the frying pan.

Kiss the children for me. Tell little Gaius that I have seen a giant, and that it was even bigger than his stories.

All my love, always,
Marcus

P.S. Please send socks. Any socks. All the socks.
